//: REPO AUDIT - deep multi-stage codebase review. Pass the codebase (or a repopack
//1: blob) as the prompt. Maps subsystems, deep-reviews each in parallel, then cross-
//2: validates to suppress the classic LLM-reviewer failure: confident-but-wrong
//3: concurrency/race claims (observed live, 2026-06). Output is a severity-ranked audit.
task: <FILL ME IN: repo or subsystem name>

stages.name: map
stages.instructions: Read the codebase in the prompt. Identify the distinct SUBSYSTEMS worth auditing separately (e.g. HTTP layer, scheduler, persistence, auth, orchestration). Output JSON {"areas": [{"name": str, "files": str (comma-separated paths/globs), "focus": str (what to scrutinize most)}, ...]}. Produce 3-6 areas; group tiny files together. Do NOT review yet - just map. Return ONLY a single JSON object with the top-level key "areas" (never a bare array, no prose).

stages.name: deep_review
stages.instructions: Audit ONLY your assigned subsystem within the codebase. Find REAL issues ranked by severity. For EACH finding emit a block: '[SEVERITY] path:symbol - issue - evidence (quote the exact code) - concrete fix'. Severity in {CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW}. Cover: correctness bugs, security (authz, injection, secret handling, data-at-rest), resource leaks / unbounded growth, error handling, and contract mismatches between this subsystem and its callers. RULE: every finding MUST quote real code as evidence - if you cannot quote it, do not report it. If you make any claim about concurrency, races, locks, or event loops, prefix it with 'UNVERIFIED-CONCURRENCY:' because these are the hardest to get right from reading alone.

stages.name: synthesize
stages.instructions: Merge all subsystem findings into ONE audit report. Deduplicate overlapping findings. DROP any finding that did not quote real code as evidence. Re-rank globally by severity. Structure: '## Critical', '## High', '## Medium', '## Low', each a list of '[path:symbol] issue - fix'. Then '## False-positive watch' listing every 'UNVERIFIED-CONCURRENCY' claim separately, marked as needs-human-verification (do NOT rank these as Critical/High). End with '## Top 3 to fix first' (the three highest-leverage real bugs) and '## Coverage' (which subsystems were reviewed).

stages.name: cross_check
stages.instructions: Adversarially check the audit. Flag: (a) any finding still lacking quoted evidence, (b) any concurrency claim NOT in the False-positive watch section, (c) duplicate findings, (d) fixes that would introduce new bugs, (e) severity inflation (a cosmetic issue marked Critical). List concrete corrections only.

stages.name: finalize
stages.instructions: Apply every cross-check correction. Move unverified concurrency claims into the False-positive watch section. Demote inflated severities. Remove evidence-free findings. Return the FULL corrected audit, preserving all section headers.

llm_judges: Does every finding outside the False-positive watch section quote or cite specific code (a path and symbol/line)?
Are all concurrency/race/lock/event-loop claims confined to the False-positive watch section (not ranked as Critical/High)?
